title: Almost all AI-Trading Bots are broken. Let me show you why.
author: tradematesHQ
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I run an stock analysis platform ([https://trademates.co](https://trademates.co/?utm_source=gemini)). This is not going to be a promo post. I want to share a concrete data-engineering post-mortem about why most "AI stock analysis" tools on the market are fundamentally broken—and the hard lesson we learned fixing it.

In our team, we have two STEM working students (physics & mathematics). Their primary job isn’t building features; it’s adversarial red-teaming: finding edge cases where our valuation and LLM scoring models get completely fooled.

About a month ago, they flagged ZVRA (Zevra Therapeutics). Our system had assigned ZVRA a very bullish score of 74/100. On paper, the financials looked solid, and recent headlines seemed calm. But when the students manually audited the underlying thesis, they found a massive flaw:

  
**The Blind Spot**

ZVRA had previously held the patent/rights to a key revenue-generating asset monetized in FY2025. In early 2026, those rights were sold off. By Q1 2026, the revenue stream disappeared. But the AI model had this still calculated for the next FY.

**Why did the AI fail to catch this?**

Standard financial news APIs (FMP, Finnhub, Polygon, Yahoo) typically fetch news for a rolling window of 90 to 180 days. By late summer, the sale of the asset in March had fallen outside that 6-month window.

The LLM received the latest financial statements (seeing a revenue increase due to the sale of the asset) and the last 90 days of news (which were completely quiet about the transaction). Without historical context, the model couldn’t reconcile why the revenue dropped—it hallucinated an operational increase instead of recognizing a planned asset divestiture.

**The Real Problem With "AI Trading Bots"**

This incident highlighted the dirty secret of the entire "AI finance" space:

**An LLM is only as good as its context window.**

99% of the so-called "AI stock pickers" and trading bots flooding Twitter and Reddit are just thin wrappers. They pull live quotes from Yahoo, grab the last 5 clickbait headlines from Google News, dump them into ChatGPT with a prompt like *"Analyze this ticker and give a Buy/Hold rating"*, and call it an algorithm.

When your data layer has a 6-month memory horizon, your model is effectively trading with amnesia. It doesn’t know about patent expirations, asset sales, CEO departures, or FDA delay notices that happened 8 months ago but dictate this year's cash flow. They aren't predicting anything—they are throwing dice with high token costs.

**How We Fixed It (And What It Actually Takes)**

We realized raw API news feeds are useless for serious models. They are 90% spam (lawsuit PRs, automated price updates) and vanish after a few months. Over the past month, we rebuilt our entire data pipeline from scratch:

1. **12-Month Deep Backfill:** For our \~4,300 active universe stocks, we now pull and store every news item and regulatory filing going back a full 365 days.
2. **Full-Text Scraping:** We don't just read headlines. A headless scraper pulls the actual full text, stripping cookie walls and boilerplate.
3. **Materiality Scoring (1–10):** An internal LLM evaluates each article:  
   * **1–3:** Routine noise (class action PRs, conference attendance).
   * **4–6:** Moderate events (analyst updates, minor partnerships).
   * **7–10:** Real valuation catalysts (guidance revisions, divestitures, clinical trial readouts, M&A).
4. **Pre-Computed Immutable Ground Truth:** Instead of scraping on the fly when a user clicks, we compile a clean, versioned JSON snapshot for each ticker. When our analysis runs, the model receives grounded, audited financials plus a pre-filtered catalyst history.

**The Takeaway**

If you are building automated financial models or evaluating AI stock tools, stop obsessing over prompt engineering or newer foundational models. We are now using this too in-house and will release it as a standalone product int he future. 

  
**The model isn't the moat. Data curation and temporal depth is the moat.** If your pipeline doesn't catch material events from 9 months ago, no amount of prompt tweaking will save your portfolio from hallucinated conclusions.

Curious to hear how others here handle multi-quarter news deduplication and catalyst tracking in their data pipelines: How deep does your historical context go, and what heuristics do you use to filter noise?
